title: Naive Bayes Quiz
description: Test your understanding of naive bayes

questions.question: What is the 'naive' assumption in Naive Bayes classification?
options: All features have the same importance
All features are conditionally independent given the class
All classes have equal prior probabilities
The data follows a normal distribution
questions.explanation: The 'naive' assumption is that all features are conditionally independent given the class label. This means P(x₁,x₂,...,xₙ|Class) = P(x₁|Class) × P(x₂|Class) × ... × P(xₙ|Class), which simplifies the computation significantly.

questions.question: In Gaussian Naive Bayes, what distribution is assumed for continuous features?
options: Uniform distribution
Exponential distribution
Normal (Gaussian) distribution
Poisson distribution
questions.explanation: Gaussian Naive Bayes assumes that continuous features follow a normal (Gaussian) distribution within each class. This allows us to model the likelihood P(feature|class) using the Gaussian probability density function.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the smoothing parameter in Naive Bayes?
options: To improve model accuracy
To prevent zero probabilities and numerical instability
To reduce overfitting
To speed up training
questions.explanation: The smoothing parameter prevents zero probabilities and numerical instability. It's added to variance calculations to ensure no feature has zero variance, and it helps avoid zero probabilities for unseen feature combinations.

questions.question: According to Bayes' theorem, P(Class|Features) is proportional to:
options: P(Features) × P(Class)
P(Features|Class) × P(Class)
P(Class) / P(Features)
P(Features) / P(Class)
questions.explanation: According to Bayes' theorem, P(Class|Features) = P(Features|Class) × P(Class) / P(Features). Since P(Features) is constant for all classes during prediction, P(Class|Features) is proportional to P(Features|Class) × P(Class).

questions.question: Why is Naive Bayes particularly effective for text classification?
options: Text features are always independent
It handles high-dimensional sparse data well
It requires no preprocessing of text data
It can only work with categorical features
questions.explanation: Naive Bayes is effective for text classification because it handles high-dimensional sparse data well. Text data often has thousands of features (words) with most being zero for any given document, and Naive Bayes performs well in such scenarios despite the independence assumption.

questions.question: What happens during the training phase of Naive Bayes?
options: It learns decision boundaries between classes
It calculates means, variances, and prior probabilities for each class
It builds a decision tree structure
It finds the optimal weights for each feature
questions.explanation: During training, Naive Bayes calculates the mean and variance of each feature for each class (for Gaussian NB), and computes the prior probability of each class. These statistics are all that's needed to make predictions later.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of Naive Bayes?
options: Fast training and prediction
Works well with small datasets
Handles feature correlations effectively
Provides probabilistic outputs
questions.explanation: Naive Bayes does NOT handle feature correlations effectively - this is actually its main limitation. The algorithm assumes features are independent, so it doesn't model correlations between features, which can hurt performance when features are highly correlated.

questions.question: In the prediction phase, how does Naive Bayes choose the final class?
options: It picks the class with the highest prior probability
It uses majority voting among features
It selects the class with the highest posterior probability
It chooses randomly among probable classes
questions.explanation: Naive Bayes chooses the class with the highest posterior probability P(Class|Features). This is calculated using Bayes' theorem by multiplying the likelihood P(Features|Class) with the prior P(Class) for each class and selecting the maximum.
